source.document: WHO SMART Guidelines — Antenatal Care (DAK L2)

declencheur: ANC.B7 Check symptoms and follow up
regle_metier: Depending on current and/or persistant symptoms, physiological symptoms counselling may be required

regles.sortie: Counselling on non-pharmacological treatments for nausea and vomiting
regles.action: Conduct counselling on physiological symptoms (see Annotations for pop-up message)
regles.annotation: Ginger, chamomile, vitamin B6 and/or acupuncture are recommended for the relief of nausea in early pregnancy, depending on a woman’s preferences and available options. Women should be informed that symptoms of nausea and vomiting usually resolve in the second half of pregnancy.
regles.reference: WHO ANC recommendations (2016): D.1. Nausea and vomiting (3) WHO consolidated self-care interventions guidelines (2019) (4)

regles.sortie: Counselling on pharmacological treatments for nausea and vomiting
regles.action: Conduct counselling on physiological symptoms (see Annotations for pop-up message)
regles.annotation: Pharmacological treatments for nausea and vomiting, such as doxylamine and metoclopramide, should be reserved for those pregnant women experiencing distressing symptoms that are not relieved by non-pharmacological options, under the supervision of a medical doctor
regles.reference: WHO ANC recommendations (2016): D.1. Nausea and vomiting (3) WHO consolidated self-care interventions guidelines (2019) (4)

regles.sortie: Counselling on diet and lifestyle changes to prevent and relieve heartburn
regles.action: Conduct counselling on physiological symptoms (see Annotations for pop-up message)
regles.annotation: Advice on diet and lifestyle is recommended to prevent and relieve heartburn in pregnancy. Antacid preparations can be offered to women with troublesome symptoms that are not relieved by lifestyle modification.
regles.reference: WHO ANC recommendations (2016): D.2. Heartburn (3) WHO consolidated self-care interventions guidelines (2019) (4)

regles.sortie: Counselling on antacid preparations to relieve heartburn
regles.action: Conduct counselling on physiological symptoms (see Annotations for pop-up message)
regles.annotation: Antacid preparations can be offered to women with troublesome symptoms that are not relieved by lifestyle modification. Magnesium carbonate and aluminium hydroxide preparations are probably unlikely to cause harm in recommended dosages.
regles.reference: WHO ANC recommendations (2016): D.2. Heartburn (3) WHO consolidated self-care interventions guidelines (2019) (4)

regles.sortie: Counselling on non-pharmacological treatment for the relief of leg cramps
regles.action: Conduct counselling on physiological symptoms (see Annotations for pop-up message)
regles.annotation: Non-pharmacological therapies, including muscle stretching, relaxation, heat therapy, dorsiflexion of the foot, and massage can be used for the relief of leg cramps in pregnancy
regles.reference: WHO ANC recommendations (2016): D.3. Leg cramps (3) WHO consolidated self-care interventions guidelines (2019) (4)

regles.sortie: Counselling on magnesium and calcium to relieve leg cramps
regles.action: Conduct counselling on physiological symptoms (see Annotations for pop-up message)
regles.annotation: If leg cramps are not relieved with non-pharmacological measures, then give 300–360 mg magnesium per day in two or three divided doses; give calcium 1 g twice daily for two weeks
regles.reference: WHO ANC recommendations (2016): D.3. Leg cramps (3) WHO consolidated self-care interventions guidelines (2019) (4)

regles.sortie: Counselling on regular exercise, physiotherapy, support belts and acupuncture to relieve low back and pelvic pain
regles.annotation: Regular exercise throughout pregnancy is recommended to prevent low back and pelvic pain. There are a number of different treatment options that can be used, such as physiotherapy, support belts and acupuncture, depending and based on a woman’s preferences and available options.
regles.reference: WHO ANC recommendations (2016): D.4. Low back and pelvic pain (3) WHO consolidated self-care interventions guidelines (2019) (4)

regles.sortie: Counselling on regular exercise, physiotherapy, support belts and acupuncture to relieve low back and pelvic pain
regles.reference: WHO ANC recommendations (2016): D.4. Low back and pelvic pain (3) WHO consolidated self-care interventions guidelines (2019) (4)

Counselling on dietary modifications to relieve constipation
regles.action: Conduct counselling on physiological symptoms (see Annotations for pop-up message)
regles.annotation: Dietary modifications to relieve constipation include promoting adequate intake of water and dietary fibre (found in vegetables, nuts, fruits and whole grains)
regles.reference: WHO ANC recommendations (2016): D.5. Constipation (3) WHO consolidated self-care interventions guidelines (2019) (4)

regles.sortie: Counselling on wheat bran or other fibre supplements to relieve constipation
regles.action: Conduct counselling on physiological symptoms (see Annotations for pop-up message)
regles.annotation: Wheat bran or other fibre supplements can be used to relieve constipation, if dietary modifications are not enough, and if they are available and appropriate
regles.reference: WHO ANC recommendations (2016): D.5. Constipation (3) WHO consolidated self-care interventions guidelines (2019) (4)

regles.sortie: Counselling on non-pharmacological options for varicose veins and oedema
regles.action: Conduct counselling on physiological symptoms (see Annotations for pop-up message)
regles.annotation: Non-pharmacological options, such as compression stockings, leg elevation and water immersion, can be used for the management of varicose veins and oedema in pregnancy, depending and based on a woman’s preferences and available options
regles.reference: WHO ANC recommendations (2016): D.6. Varicose veins and oedema (3) WHO consolidated self-care interventions guidelines (2019) (4)
